phenomenon_scale.description: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength at the detail cellular scale

law.name: Turing wavenumber k_c
law.formula: k_c = argmax_k Re(eig(gamma J - k^2 D)), lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c
law.kinetics: Schnakenberg: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
law.anisotropic_diffusion: partial_t u = Du_x u_xx + Du_y u_yy + gamma f; partial_t v = Dv_x v_xx + Dv_y v_yy + gamma g

parameters.note: gamma and Dv_y place the dorsoventral dispersion peak on k = 2 pi / 24.08 µm. Anisotropy 3.85 is the Holocene D. rerio value; 1.12 is the D. nigrofasciatus spot regime at the same cellular scale. These are not the 1 mm Quigley-slot parameters and not the 18 µm Yamanaka-slot parameters.

chronospecies_delta.what_changes: At 24.08 µm and 0 Ma the terminal species raises inhibitor anisotropy from 1.12 to 3.85. The AP Turing margin changes sign (unstable to stable) while the DV margin stays positive, so the selected pattern changes from spots to horizontal stripes whose wavelength is 24.08 µm. There is no successor chronospecies.
reported_in_source: Nakamasu et al. 2009: melanophore-xanthophore short-range activation and long-range inhibition satisfy Turing conditions on zebrafish skin.
Hiscock & Megason 2015: tissue anisotropy orients a Turing pattern by moving one axis out of the unstable band.
Quigley et al. 2004 and Patterson et al. 2014: D. nigrofasciatus deploys a broken-stripe / spot pattern relative to D. rerio stripes.

empirical_claims.claim: Zebrafish stripe maintenance is a Turing interaction between melanophores and xanthophores.
Anisotropic diffusion or growth orients Turing stripes by restricting the unstable wavevector.
Melanophore-xanthophore interaction at this tier is contact-range, tens of micrometres, not the adult millimetre stripe period.
